story.head: Tired legs for the Avalanche
paras: The Ducks (10-8-1) lost 4-2 to Nashville on Nov 11, and the Avalanche (11-6-3) lost 4-3 in overtime to Ottawa on Nov 12. The Avalanche played last night, and the Ducks are rested. Going in, the Ducks are third in the Pacific (tied for 16th in the NHL) and the Avalanche third in the Central (tied for 11th).
The Ducks’ record (.553) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.496), largely thanks to their finishing. The Avalanche’s record (.625) is about what their chances are worth.

The Ducks forecheck as hard as almost anyone (2nd), hit a lot (2nd) and give up a lot of dangerous shots (31st). Anaheim has allowed 3.68 goals a game, the third most in the league. As for the Avalanche, they get their defensemen shooting (1st) and do a lot of their shooting from distance (lowest). Colorado has scored 4.05 goals a game, the second most in the league. The Avs are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Ducks. Beyond that, both teams like to play fast, especially the Avalanche (1st), so expect an open game.

Leo Carlsson (6 G / 20 A / 26 P in 19 GP) leads the Ducks in scoring, with five goals in eight games against Colorado since 2023-24. Cutter Gauthier (16 G / 7 A / 23 P in 18 GP) has a team-high 16 goals, tied for third in the NHL, with eleven points in his last five games. For the Avalanche, Martin Nečas (10 G / 14 A / 24 P in 20 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Artturi Lehkonen (14 G / 5 A / 19 P in 20 GP) has a team-high 14 goals, fifth in the NHL.

Laurent Brossoit (4-1-0 / .866 SV% in 5 GS) has struggled for Anaheim so far, but will likely start. Scott Wedgewood (1-3-2 / .863 SV% in 6 GS) has struggled for Colorado so far, but will likely start. Wedgewood has a .947 save percentage in five starts against the Ducks, well above his usual .904. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
The Avalanche usually control more of the chances than the Ducks do.

items.text: The Ducks have been without A.J. Greer and Tyson Hinds for several games.
The Avalanche are newly without Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team is missing more right now.
Cutter Gauthier has a point in nine straight games, with a goal in each of the last seven.
Artturi Lehkonen has 14 goals on chances worth about 7.2 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
